Sharp recovery through July on earnings, rotation
Global funds shifted from AI chips to IT
Nasdaq chip selloff pushed money into Indian IT
Q1 FY27 earnings season drove sector gains
HCLTech guidance hold surprised the Street positively
Infosys guidance trim triggered brief profit booking
Sector sharply outperformed Nifty 50 in July
Coforge, Persistent led mid-cap IT rally
Still down sharply on a 2026 year-to-date basis

sector_news_last_month: Nifty IT touched a fresh 52-week low on 1 July, marking the trough of a painful multi-month correction
From that low, the index staged a sharp recovery through July, becoming one of the best-performing NSE sectoral indices for the month

A major driver was global capital rotating out of AI-linked semiconductor stocks in South Korea, Japan and Taiwan and into IT services names, seen as safer since they earn revenue from services rather than AI hardware
A sharp Nasdaq selloff in semiconductor stocks on AI-valuation jitters reinforced this rotation into Indian IT
Q1 FY27 earnings season ran through the month, with nearly every major IT company reporting results and setting stock-specific direction within the broader rally

Results were broadly mixed to positive: several companies showed resilient or improving margins and strong deal-win momentum, even as revenue growth stayed generally muted amid ongoing global macro uncertainty
Guidance commentary was a key swing factor - names that held or reaffirmed full-year guidance were rewarded, while any guidance trims triggered short-lived profit booking
Despite the strong monthly bounce, the sector remained deeply negative on a year-to-date basis for 2026, having underperformed the broader market by a wide margin over the year as a whole
Markets also stayed watchful of the US Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision through the month, an important cross-current for global risk sentiment and FII flows into Indian IT

AI itself was a double-edged theme for the sector - a source of new deal wins and revenue for IT services companies, but also the trigger for the semiconductor-linked volatility that shaped flows into and out of the sector
